note: Per-crate supply-chain AUDIT state (paragon axis 1: 'every third-party dependency verified'). This is the per-crate human/imported attestation layer that complements the cargo-deny GATE recorded in data/dep_boundary_state.json. cargo-deny checks advisories/licenses/bans/sources over the whole graph; cargo-vet adds per-crate audit attestation: each third-party crate-version is either (a) covered by a trusted imported audit registry (Mozilla/Google/Bytecode Alliance/Embark/ISRG/Zcash), (b) audited locally in supply-chain/audits.toml, or (c) carried as an exemption (the unaudited baseline snapshotted by `cargo vet init`). Goal is a MONOTONIC tracker: the audited fraction only rises (exemptions only shrink) as more crates are covered by imports or locally audited. ENFORCEMENT: a SOFT/informational `cargo vet` step in scripts/local_gate.sh (FULL mode) prints coverage % and the unaudited count as a tracked metric — it is intentionally NOT a hard fail-closed gate while exemptions remain, so it does not block every push.
supply_chain_dir: supply-chain/ (config.toml + audits.toml + imports.lock — audit attestations only, ~70KB; NOT vendored crate source)
scope_note: First-party code is OUT of scope for third-party accounting: cargo-vet treats the 27 clean workspace crates and the ../ay path-dep stack (69 path packages incl ../ay) as first-party/exempt-by-source. The audit accounting below covers ONLY the crates.io registry third-party crates.
vet_status: Vetting Succeeded (exemptions cover the unaudited remainder; cargo vet exits 0)

coverage_package_versions.comment: cargo-vet's authoritative count is by crate-VERSION over the default-target resolved graph (this is what the gate reports).

coverage_by_crate_name.comment: Deduplicated by crate NAME across versions (a coarser but more intuitive headline).

trusted_imports.comment: Standard, widely-used cargo-vet audit registries pulled into supply-chain/imports.lock. These are the 'verified by reputable third parties' layer. 257 imported audit records + 7 trusted publishers were resolved against our graph.

highest_risk_unaudited.comment: These are exemption-only (NOT covered by any trusted import) and carry the largest native-C/FFI or unsafe surface — the priority targets for the next local audit pass.

native_c_ffi.why: C zstd bindings (build.rs compiles vendored C)
raw FFI to the system libc; huge unsafe surface
FFI to OS entropy syscalls; security-critical
runtime CPU feature detection via asm/FFI

large_unsafe_surface.why: core hashmap with raw-pointer unsafe internals
SIMD byte search with unsafe intrinsics

vendoring_status.summary: cargo-vet records audit ATTESTATIONS only (small supply-chain/ dir). It does NOT vendor crate source. The VENDORING half of axis 1 is now implemented as tooling + a release artifact (NOT committed to git), resolving the prior 'deferred' decision.
vendoring_status.implemented: A `cargo vendor --versioned-dirs vendor/` tree (385 crates: 384 crates.io + 1 git carcara, ~522.6MB source -> ~63MB tar.zst) is produced as an OFFLINE-REPRODUCIBLE, TAMPER-EVIDENT artifact. Following the repo's release-artifact convention (like .mathverse shards / mathverse-library-v*.tar.zst), the vendor/ tree is GITIGNORED and published as vendor-sources-v*.tar.zst, NOT committed. See docs/SUPPLY_CHAIN_VENDORING.md.
vendoring_status.tamper_evidence: data/vendor_manifest.json pins every vendored crate by name+version+checksum. crates.io crates use the registry sha256 (asserted equal to Cargo.lock's `checksum =` at generation time); the git crate uses a deterministic sha256 over cargo's per-file checksum map. Regenerate with scripts/gen_vendor_manifest.py and diff to detect source drift.
vendoring_status.offline_wiring: OPT-IN via .cargo/config.offline.toml (NEVER the default .cargo/config.toml — that would force vendored resolution and break checkouts lacking the gitignored tree). Invoked via `cargo --config .cargo/config.offline.toml --offline ...` or scripts/build_offline.sh. Verified: default online build unchanged; offline build resolves + compiles clean-kernel from vendor/.
vendoring_status.package_verify: scripts/package_vendor.sh {package,verify} tar.zst's the tree with a sha256 sidecar and a re-extract+re-checksum verify step, mirroring crates/clean-mathverse/src/release.rs's package/verify pattern.

enforcement.gate: scripts/local_gate.sh — FULL mode only, SOFT/informational (warn mode, never fail-closed while exemptions remain)
enforcement.ratchet_contract: audited fraction monotonic-up / exemption count monotonic-down. Regenerate after any dep-graph change or new local audit; re-run `cargo vet` + the by-name accounting and update this file. A future hard-gate flip is possible once exemptions reach 0.

follow_ups: Locally audit the 9 highest-risk unaudited crates (5 native-C/FFI + 4 large-unsafe) in supply-chain/audits.toml to shrink the exemption set where no trusted import exists.
Re-import the trusted registries periodically (cargo vet import --update) to pick up newly-published audits and shrink exemptions for free.

Vendoring DONE (release-artifact convention): vendor/ gitignored, published as vendor-sources-v*.tar.zst, tamper-evidence in data/vendor_manifest.json. Regenerate the vendor tree + manifest on any Cargo.lock change (cargo vendor --versioned-dirs vendor/ && python3 scripts/gen_vendor_manifest.py); see docs/SUPPLY_CHAIN_VENDORING.md.
